original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: At g=13 and q=8, in the first-stage internal gap, no constant thin maps meet the paired-star endpoint when the off-diagonal block B is nonzero. The five rank-8 maps forced by every D_j=1 sum to that unique matrix and fail. Both half orders are included.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed query demand removes real work. This session takes the interleaved remainder of open PR #7010: one pattern that separates the halves of stage 0, the constant thin maps forced by setting every D_j=1, and the normalized coefficient at two field points. The adjacent-halves theorem does not apply to this pattern.
bottleneck_link: Five rank-8 maps meet the chronological floor of 40 and escape the adjacent-halves count. On this pattern the normalized leaf-to-leaf block is a nonzero scalar times B, so the word does not supply a caller or a change to the selected frontier 781451/250000000.
stop_rule: Stop after the block identity for this one pattern, both half orders, and the two field points. Do not search a second gap, a later open stage, nested calls, or g=31.
evidence: PROOF.md derives the leaf-to-leaf block (D0+1) D_t^{-1} B. verify.py checks the legal pair, the five rank-8 bundles, the D_j=1 endpoint, and both half orders at two GF(16) points. It prints PASS_PAIRED_STAR_G13_Q8_INTERNAL_GAP. Python 3.12, standard library only.

open_questions.question: Can one of the five rank-8 maps sit in the gap after stage 0 and cancel the leaf-0 from leaf-1 block, while the sum at every D_j=1 stays the same swap?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every thin map in this package shares one internal conjugation. A map in the next gap is scaled only by completed stage factors, so its leaf-to-leaf block carries a different monomial. That is the smallest split of this pattern, and it is not the consecutive schedule.
open_questions.first_step: Subtract a rank-8 matrix supported on the two leaf-0/leaf-1 blocks of B from the internal sum, add that matrix after stage 0, and recompute the leaf-0 from leaf-1 block at D=(2,3,...,14).
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The calculation changes the one-gap support used here.

open_questions.question: Does the same block stay nonzero when stage 0 is not the first stage, so an earlier adjacent stage has already scaled the state?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The open stage here is first, so no scalar prefix stands in front of the half conjugation. An earlier stage multiplies blocks by monomials before that conjugation.
open_questions.first_step: Complete stage 1 as an adjacent pair, open stage 0 around the same five maps, and read the leaf-0 from leaf-2 block at one point with D_1 not equal to 1.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The word order is the one change.
